text.en: A magic box multiplies every number put into it. Out come 28, 36, 48 and 72. Can you guess the multiplier? It could be 1, 2 or 4 - and more than one works! Today we find out why.

Look at the numbers that came out of the box: 28, 36, 48 and 72.
The multipliers 1, 2 and 4 work for all of them. These are the common factors of the four numbers.
The numbers 28, 36, 48 and 72 are multiples of 1, 2 and 4. The product of two or more factors gives a multiple.
A number arranged in an array shows its factors. For 15, make 3 rows of 5 squares: 3 x 5 = 15, so 3 and 5 are factors and 15 is their multiple.
Make arrays for 12: 3 x 4, 2 x 6 and 1 x 12. So the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
12 is a multiple of each of these factors. Every number is a multiple of itself, and 1 and the number itself are always factors.
A number like 13 or 37 has only two factors, 1 and itself. Such numbers are called prime numbers. Try making arrays for 13 and you will see only one array, 1 x 13.
Not every number has many factors. 15 has four factors: 1, 3, 5 and 15 - so only two arrays, 1 x 15 and 3 x 5.

Find pairs that multiply to 20: 1 x 20, 2 x 10, 4 x 5.

why.en: Try dividing 20 by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and keep those with no remainder.

text.en: Write the numbers from the pairs in order: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20.

why.en: Each number in a pair is a factor.

text.en: 20 is a multiple of every one of these factors.

why.en: If 4 x 5 = 20, then 20 is a multiple of 4 and of 5.

prompt.en: What is the difference between a factor and a multiple? Use 12 to explain.

requiredIdeas.en: 12 has factors 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 and is a multiple of each

points.en: Factors are the numbers that divide a number completely; multiples are what we get by multiplying.
An array shows factor pairs: 3 x 4 = 12 means 3 and 4 are factors of 12.
1 and the number itself are factors of every number; a number with only these two factors is prime.
Common factors of 28, 36, 48 and 72 include 1, 2 and 4.
